mcqs.question: Which of the following quantities is a vector?
mcqs.explanation: Displacement has both magnitude and direction, making it a vector. Speed, mass, and temperature are scalars because they possess only magnitude and no specific direction.

mcqs.question: In a diagram, an arrow drawn from point O to point P has a length proportional to its magnitude and an arrowhead indicating its direction. Which description correctly represents a vector of magnitude 5 units pointing east?

options.A: Arrow of length 5 units pointing east
options.B: Arrow of length 5 units pointing north
options.C: Arrow of length 3 units pointing east
options.D: Arrow of length 5 units pointing west

mcqs.answer: Arrow of length 5 units pointing east
mcqs.explanation: A vector is shown by an arrow whose length indicates magnitude and whose arrowhead shows direction. Option A matches both the required magnitude (5 units) and direction (east). The other options either have the wrong direction or wrong magnitude.

mcqs.question: A student claims that the speed of a car is a vector because it tells how fast the car is moving. Which statement best addresses this misconception?

options.A: The statement is correct; speed is a vector.
options.B: The statement is incorrect; speed is a scalar because it has no direction.
options.C: Speed becomes a vector when the car changes direction.
options.D: Speed is a vector only in circular motion.

mcqs.answer: The statement is incorrect; speed is a scalar because it has no direction.
mcqs.explanation: Speed measures how fast an object moves and has only magnitude, so it is a scalar. Velocity, which includes direction, is the vector counterpart. Options A, C, and D incorrectly treat speed as a vector.

mcqs.question: Which of the following quantities is NOT a vector?
mcqs.explanation: Force, velocity, and acceleration each have magnitude and a specific direction, making them vectors. Energy is defined only by its magnitude (e.g., joules) and has no direction, so it is a scalar.

mcqs.question: Consider the following pairs of physical quantities. Identify the pair in which both quantities are vectors.
mcqs.explanation: Both displacement and velocity possess magnitude and a specific direction, qualifying them as vectors. Speed, distance, mass, temperature, and pressure are scalars; weight, while having direction, is paired with mass (a scalar) in option C, making the pair mixed.

mcqs.question: Vector A is represented by an arrow of length 3 cm making an angle of 30° with the positive x‑axis. Which arrow correctly represents the vector 2A?
mcqs.explanation: Multiplying a vector by 2 doubles its magnitude while keeping its direction unchanged. Hence, 2A has twice the length (6 cm) and the same angle (30°). Options B, C, and D either change the direction or fail to double the magnitude.

mcqs.question: In the context of vectors, what do the terms magnitude and direction refer to?

options.A: The size (length) of the vector and the orientation in space
options.D: The force and its point of application

mcqs.answer: The size (length) of the vector and the orientation in space
mcqs.explanation: Magnitude is the scalar length of the vector, while direction specifies the line along which the vector points. The other options describe unrelated physical concepts.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
mcqs.explanation: Momentum (mass × velocity) has both magnitude and direction, making it a vector. Work, power, and electric charge are scalars; they are described solely by magnitude.
